scientific_question: Is nine-slot retained assignment cache still beneficial under faster circular geometry drift, or does staleness erase its prior advantage?
hypothesis: A legality-filtered, history-only cache may lose churn benefit when cell-home changes by five cells per episode rather than one. Both benefit and harm are valid outcomes.
freeze: Commit this exact configuration before adding/activating workflow or original execution; no post-result retuning of drift, cache, seeds, episodes, learning or criteria.
population: Exactly sixteen motif identities/cells, seven active, up to nine cached inactive assignments, eight episodes/seed, radius-two circular neighbors, same active generator and four-key home collision pattern inherited from Y025.
changed_delta: Only base home uses (7*key+seed+5*episode) mod16 instead of (7*key+seed+episode) mod16; cache/matcher and policies unchanged with exact Y025 source identity.
arms: matched-cache sham writes nine-slot cache but cannot read for matching
cache-read arm writes identical cache and uses only legal previously observed placements
primary: Heldout per-seed churn difference sham-cache, along with cardinality, search calls, matched write counts, legal cache-read hits; REPEATED_DRIFT_BENEFIT if all four seeds save churn; STALENESS_HARM if aggregate savings negative; MIXED otherwise (includes no gain).
independent_validation: Independent exhaustive Hall bound for seven active keys; cache write and occupancy equality between arms; deterministic repeated output; exact parent/prereg/science blobs; one full repo regression.
claim_limit: Synthetic episodic assignment retention under geometry drift, not learning, real-world developmental adaptation, or accepted-reference mutation.
